record.context_brief: geometric flag orbits in convex polytopes
record.original_question: For which pairs of integers (k, d) does there exist a convex d-polytope with exactly k geometric flag orbits?

evidence.quote: Problem 27. For what values of k and d is there a convex d-polytope with k geometric flag orbits?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let P be a convex d-dimensional polytope in Euclidean space. A flag of P is a maximal chain F_0 < F_1 < ... < F_{d-1} of nonempty proper faces of P, where F_i has dimension i. The Euclidean symmetry group G(P) of P acts on the set F(P) of flags of P; the orbits of this action are called the geometric flag orbits of P. Say that P is geometrically k-orbit if |F(P)/G(P)| = k.

Determine all pairs of positive integers (k, d) for which there exists a convex d-polytope that is geometrically k-orbit.
artifact.status_search_result: The general classification problem remains open. Partial results are known: regular (1-orbit) convex polytopes are classified in all dimensions; geometrically 2-orbit convex polytopes exist only in dimensions 2 and 3 and have been classified; geometrically 3-orbit convex polytopes are known to exist in dimensions 2 through 8 with classification results in low dimensions. Beyond these, the full set of admissible (k,d) is not determined.

status_evidence.title: Convex Polytopes and Tilings with Few Flag Orbits
status_evidence.snippet: Two-orbit convex polytopes exist only in two or three dimensions; three-orbit convex polytopes exist in two through eight dimensions.
status_evidence.claim: Partial classifications exist for k=2 and k=3.

status_evidence.title: Two-Orbit Convex Polytopes and Tilings
status_evidence.snippet: Convex polytopes with two flag orbits exist only in 2 and 3 dimensions; classification given.
